topic: verification before completion in agent workflows
audience_job: Ship an LLM feature without claiming it works before a reproducible run
label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS

theses.thesis: Throughput gains shift the bottleneck from generation to verification
theses.evidence: PagedAttention raises batch throughput by reusing KV cache blocks
theses.counterexample: A benchmark with no correctness assertion reports only tokens per second
theses.reader_action: Add an output assertion to the serving benchmark before quoting speed

theses.thesis: A completion claim is stronger than a rendering claim only when it has a receipt
theses.evidence: The workflow records gate history and publish receipts instead of status words
theses.counterexample: A dashboard marked green by a fallback that never called the provider
theses.reader_action: Require a command output file for every stage marked advanced

theses.thesis: Agent pipelines need refusal states more than optimistic defaults
theses.evidence: The X gate refuses packaging until a human review exists
theses.counterexample: An orchestrator that silently degrades a failed check to a pass
theses.reader_action: Name the blocker in the receipt and stop the chain instead of guessing

red_team: Throughput was measured on a different GPU and batch size, so the ratio does not transfer to this host.
A fast wrong answer can be caught by sampling, but sampling is not a proof of correctness.
The receipt proves a command ran; it does not prove a person approved the claim.

parts: vLLM makes token serving fast. Speed changes the cost of a mistake, not the need to catch it. The gate is the receipt: run the command, read the output, then say done. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm

image_brief: A dark card pairing throughput with the need for verification receipts
alt_text: A dark blue card states that fast token serving does not prove a correct answer, and asks for a reproducible receipt.
